assertions.text: Output contains a @TableTest annotation
assertions.evidence: Found @TableTest annotation

assertions.text: Multiple @TableTest methods are used, each addressing a distinct concern — not one monolithic table mixing all splitting rules.
assertions.evidence: Four @TableTest methods: splitsShipmentsByFulfillmentTypeAndAddress, splitsShipmentsByStockAvailability, choosesWarehouseCombinationMinimizingShipmentCount, keepsCompanionProductsTogetherWhenPossible

assertions.text: Cell values make the rule falsifiable, not merely distinguishable.
assertions.evidence: First @TableTest has rows with identical expectation format but varying inputs (e.g., 'Same fulfillment type and address' vs 'Same type, different delivery addresses' both produce list outputs). However, the availability table's expectations are all string-encoded (e.g., 'IMMEDIATE:[camera,lens]') making them non-falsifiable by simple value comparison—an implementation returning fixed strings would pass.

assertions.text: A reader can state the rule from the table alone, without the test method body.
assertions.evidence: @Description annotations explicitly state key assumptions: 'BACKORDERED and PRE_ORDERED both ship WHEN_AVAILABLE' and 'WarehouseInventory.addCompanionGroup' is the source of truth. Column headers and cell values are self-contained.

assertions.text: Each @TableTest has only the rows needed to express its concern's rules — no unnecessary permutations from combining concerns.
assertions.evidence: Fulfillment/address table has 6 rows; the reference decomposition requires only 5 (same type+address, different addresses, delivery vs pickup, two pickups, and one composition case). The extra row 'Delivery split by address, plus a separate pickup item' cross-multiplies concerns.

assertions.text: Fulfillment method splitting is represented in a @TableTest — its own, or one shared with the delivery-address split — showing that items with different fulfillment types (store pickup vs home delivery) cannot share a shipment.
assertions.evidence: splitsShipmentsByFulfillmentTypeAndAddress includes row 'Delivery and pickup items always split' with camera (DELIVERY) and mug (PICKUP) producing separate shipments.

assertions.text: Delivery address splitting is represented in a @TableTest — its own, or one shared with the fulfillment-method split — showing that items going to different addresses must be in separate shipments.
assertions.evidence: splitsShipmentsByFulfillmentTypeAndAddress includes row 'Same type, different delivery addresses' with camera (Addr-A) and watch (Addr-B) producing separate shipments.

assertions.text: Availability splitting is represented as its own @TableTest — in-stock items ship immediately, backordered/pre-ordered items ship when available.
assertions.evidence: splitsShipmentsByStockAvailability has 6 rows including 'In-stock item not held for a backordered item' and 'Backordered and pre-ordered items combine' demonstrating the two-state model.

assertions.text: Warehouse allocation (minimising shipments) is represented as its own @TableTest — choosing which warehouses to ship from to minimise total shipment count.
assertions.evidence: choosesWarehouseCombinationMinimizingShipmentCount has 4 rows including 'Correct warehouse pair must be found, not just any pair' with camera/lens/mic/battery requiring W1+W3, not W1+W2 or W2+W3.

assertions.text: Companion product grouping is represented as its own @TableTest — paired items (e.g. camera body and lens) should ship together from the same location when possible.
assertions.evidence: keepsCompanionProductsTogetherWhenPossible has 3 rows: 'Companions win a tie', 'Companions split when no warehouse stocks both', and 'Companions already together needs no trade-off'.

assertions.text: Each @TableTest method includes all output columns for its concern in the same table — e.g. warehouse allocation includes both the assignment and shipment count, not split across methods.
assertions.evidence: Each @TableTest has a single 'Shipments?' output column capturing the complete result; warehouse and companion tables include warehouse IDs in the shipment descriptions.

assertions.text: A compound output — a collection of items, or items keyed by a tag — is expressed as a native TableTest list, map, or set (possibly nested, e.g. [[a, b], [c]] or [W1: [a, b]]), not as a hand-rolled string that encodes the structure with embedded brackets or colons (e.g. "W1:[a,b]") and is assembled or parsed by a helper. FAILS when an expectation cell packs multiple values into one quoted scalar that the test builds via a stringifying helper. PASSES when the output column is a native collection — sets for order-independent semantics, or ordered lists/maps with a canonical sort. Scalar outputs (a number, an enum, or a single message) are exempt.
assertions.evidence: Expected shipments use string encoding like ["W1:[camera,lens,mic]"] and ["IMMEDIATE:[camera,lens]"] built by describeByWarehouse/describeByAvailability helpers, not native TableTest collections like [W1: {camera, lens, mic}].

assertions.evidence: First column(s): "Scenario", "Scenario", "Scenario", "Scenario"

assertions.text: At least one output column name ends with '?' (e.g. 'Shipments?', 'Groups?')
assertions.evidence: Question-mark columns: Shipments?, Shipments?, Shipments?, Shipments?

assertions.text: Scenario names describe the business situation (e.g. 'Consolidate: two beats three', 'Everything at one warehouse') — not 'Test case 2'.
assertions.evidence: All scenario names describe business conditions: 'Same fulfillment type and address', 'In-stock item not held for a backordered item', 'Correct warehouse pair must be found, not just any pair', 'Companions win a tie between equally minimal warehouses'.

assertions.text: Column names use business/domain language (e.g. 'Shipments?' not 'Result?', 'Warehouse stock' not 'inventory_map'). The tables read as a specification a product person could review.
assertions.evidence: Column names are 'Items', 'Shipments?', 'W1 Stock', 'W2 Stock', 'W3 Stock', 'Companions' — all domain language, with '?' suffix on output columns per TableTest convention.
